exposure: personal experiences of a difficult birth
cesarean delivery instead of planned vaginal delivery
cohort: The study included 205 healthy women surveyed before giving birth (at 37+ gestational weeks) and then again 2 weeks and 2 months after childbirth.
finding: Factors such as miscarriages, difficult birth experiences, unplanned cesarean delivery, epidural anesthesia, and financial satisfaction were significantly associated with depressive symptoms during pregnancy and the postpartum period, with relationship quality also showing a significant correlation.
mod_finding: Personal experiences of a difficult birth, cesarean delivery instead of planned vaginal delivery, and the application of epidural anesthesia were significantly associated with the presence of depressive symptoms in the second week after childbirth.
gest_age: 37+ gestational weeks (at the time of initial survey)
